SOURCE: RA-DIT: Retrieval-Augmented Dual Instruction Tuning. Xi Victoria Lin, Xilun Chen, Mingda Chen, Weijia Shi, Maria Lomeli, Rich James, Pedro Rodriguez, Jacob Kahn, Gergely Szilvasy, Mike Lewis, Luke Zettlemoyer, Scott Yih (FAIR at Meta). ICLR 2024 (arXiv:2310.01352v4, May 2024; file is lin-2023-ra-dit.pdf).

COVERAGE: 95,915 of 95,915 chars read (all 25+ pages incl. appendices A-F). References skimmed only. Extraction is clean. Figures 1 and 2 are images, so I could not read their data. Their captions came from the text and I did not run figures.py.

NOTE ON TARGET NOTE: Note 11 does not cite RA-DIT (its sources are Yan 2024, HyDE, DPO, REPLUG). The closest hooks are the REPLUG/LSR paragraph in item 5, the "fine-tuning before you have data" pitfall, and CRAG (which compares to Self-RAG). RA-DIT is a direct extension of REPLUG LSR, so it sharpens that paragraph.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Fine-tuning both LM and retriever beats off-the-shelf REPLUG on knowledge-intensive tasks.
  number: +8.9 (0-shot), +1.4 (5-shot) avg points
  setup: LLaMA 65B, DRAGON+ retriever, 399M-chunk corpus, top-10 chunks ensembled, avg over MMLU/NQ/TQA/ELI5, test sets. 0-shot avg 43.1 -> 50.5; 5-shot 52.7 -> 55.2 (Table 2).
  quote: "RA-DIT significantly outperforms REPLUG (+8.9% in 0-shot and +1.4% in 5-shot on average over MMLU, NQ, TQA and ELI5)"
  where: p.6, section 4

- Gain over untuned in-context RALM on single datasets.
  number: NQ +22 (0-shot), +3.8 (5-shot); MMLU +8.2 / +0.7
  setup: as above, RA-DIT 65B vs REPLUG. Table 2: NQ 28.8 -> 35.2 (0-shot) and 42.3 -> 43.9 (5-shot). Introduction's percentages do not match the Table 2 point differences (6.4 and 1.6). They are probably relative gains, so flag this.
  quote: "Natural Questions (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019) (+22% 0-shot; +3.8% 5-shot)"
  where: p.2, Introduction

- Against ATLAS 11B, 64-shot fine-tuned, RA-DIT 65B wins on average.
  number: +4.1 points (60.9 vs 56.8); wins on 6 of 8 datasets
  setup: 8 KILT-style tasks. RA-DIT uses ONE multi-task model fine-tuned on 64 examples per task combined. ATLAS fine-tunes per task. ATLAS is 11B and RA-DIT is 65B, so the sizes are not matched.
  quote: "despite using a single model, RA-DIT outperforms ATLAS by an average of 4.1 points, achieving higher performance on 6 out of the 8 datasets."
  where: p.6

- Each half of the dual tuning helps and the combination helps most, but the gains are small on the dev sets.
  number: Table 6, 5-shot dev avg: baseline 53.8, FTed retriever only 54.4, LM-ft only 53.9, both 54.6
  setup: LLaMA 65B, 10 dev tasks, 5-shot. The paper's own wording is that RA-DIT "outperforms the REPLUG baseline by 0.8 points on average". LM-ft alone gains only 0.1 avg, though it helps more in 0-shot (Table 4).
  quote: "the most gain can be achieved when combining LM-ft and R-ft in our RA-DIT method, which outperforms the REPLUG baseline by 0.8 points on average."
  where: p.8, section 5.2, Table 6

- Retrieval-augmented instruction tuning (RA-IT) beats ordinary instruction tuning (IT) at 0-shot with retrieval, and the gap closes at 5-shot.
  number: 51.0 vs 47.7 avg (top-10 chunks, 0-shot); 5-shot 55.8 vs 55.6
  setup: LLaMA 65B + DRAGON+, 6 KILT dev tasks (Table 4). Without retrieval, the RA-IT 0-shot average is 29.0 and IT is 24.9. Plain instruction tuning gave marginal or negative effects at 5-shot, except on HotpotQA.
  quote: "In the 0-shot setting with top-10 retrieved chunks, the RA-IT 65B model outperforms the IT 65B model by a large margin (51.0% vs. 47.7%)."
  where: p.7, section 5.1, Table 4

- Training the LM with retrieved chunks, including wrong ones, teaches it to ignore bad retrievals and lean on its own knowledge.
  number: none (qualitative, via examples)
  setup: k~=3 retrieved chunks per example, each as a separate training instance. SQuAD v2 in the mix teaches "I don't know" on irrelevant passages. Appendix F HotpotQA 0-shot examples show IT 65B misled by distractors and saying "I don't know" more often.
  quote: "By training the LLM to make correct predictions when a wrong retrieved chunk is given, we enable the LLM to ignore misleading retrieval content and lean into its parametric knowledge in such cases."
  where: p.4, 2.3. Examples in App. F, pp.24-25

- Retriever fine-tuning with LM supervision (LSR) gives small gains, and the data mix matters.
  number: corpus-only +0.4; MTI-only +0.1; 95% corpus + 5% MTI +0.6 avg points over DRAGON+
  setup: LLaMA 65B, 5-shot dev, Table 5 (avg of 6 KILT dev tasks: 57.4 base, 58.0 best). Retrieval-corpus data = 900k chunks, first 50 tokens as input, last 50 as target. MTI = 286k examples from 10 QA/dialog tasks. Retriever recipe: tau = 0.01, top-10 chunks scored by LLaMA 65B, lr 1e-5, one epoch, 16 A100s.
  quote: "fine-tuning with “95% corpus data + 5% MTI data” achieves the best accuracy across all models, outperforming the non-finetuned baseline by 0.6 points on average."
  where: p.7-8, 5.1; App. B p.20

- Update only the query encoder, not both encoders.
  number: avg 57.8 (query only) vs 55.8 (both encoders), 5-shot dev, corpus data
  setup: same Table 5. Doc embeddings stay fixed, so the index need not be re-embedded.
  quote: "freezing the document encoder produces significantly better performance."
  where: p.8; Table 5; App. B (p.20, "there is no need to update the chunk embeddings")

- Retrieval lifts small models more. A 7B model with more than one retrieved chunk surpasses vanilla 65B on several tasks.
  number: none stated (figure only)
  setup: RA-IT 7B/13B/65B + DRAGON+, dev tasks, Fig. 2. Larger models still lead on multi-hop tasks (HotpotQA, WoW).
  quote: "the 7B model leveraging > 1 retrieved chunks surpassed the performance of the vanilla 65B model on several tasks."
  where: p.21, App. E.1

- Retriever choice matters under a fixed LM.
  number: 5-shot dev avg: Contriever 47.5, Contriever-msmarco 51.8, DRAGON+ 53.4, no retrieval 45.0
  setup: LLaMA 65B, REPLUG setting, 399M corpus (Table 7)
  quote: "All retrieval-augmented models substantially improve over the LLAMA baseline, and DRAGON + significantly outperforms both Contriever and Contriever-MSMARCO."
  where: p.8, 5.3

- Corpus choice matters, and the model follows the index it is given.
  number: 5-shot dev avg: Wiki 2021 54.7, Wiki 2021 + infobox 54.8, Wiki 2018 51.9, CC only 47.0
  setup: LLaMA 65B + DRAGON+ (Table 14). The wide gaps are on zsRE and T-REx, where CC-only scored 30.3 and 46.2 against 65.3 and 73.1 for Wiki 2021. Wiki 2018 does better on NQ (42.6 vs 41.8).
  quote: "This indicates that our retrieval-augmented LM is faithful to the supplied retrieval corpus, and up-to-date information can be provided by updating the retrieval index at test time."
  where: p.23, App. E.3

- Parallel per-chunk encoding is about as good as concatenating chunks.
  number: 50.1 (parallel) vs 50.9 (concat), 0-shot, top-3
  setup: RA-IT 65B, 6 KILT dev tasks (Table 13). The model was trained with parallel prompts, which may favour that configuration.
  quote: "the two approaches perform closely on average with chunk concatenation demonstrating a small benefit."
  where: p.23, App. E.2

- Tuning for retrieval does not damage the LM's non-retrieval abilities.
  number: commonsense 0-shot avg 72.1 -> 74.5; improved on 7 of 8 datasets (OBQA fell, 60.2 -> 58.8)
  setup: LLaMA 65B vs RA-DIT 65B, no retrieval, Table 3
  quote: "RA-DIT demonstrates improvements over the base LLAMA models on 7 out of 8 evaluation datasets"
  where: p.6

- Iterative dual tuning gave no further gain.
  number: none
  setup: one or two iterations in preliminary experiments, not reported in tables
  quote: "did not observe further gains."
  where: p.8, 5.2

LIMITS
- Retriever gains are small (0.1 to 0.6 points on dev averages). Most of the benefit comes from LM-ft and from having retrieval at all.
- Setup is heavy. LM-ft used 8, 16 and 64 A100s for 7B, 13B and 65B. R-ft used 16 A100s. All of this is LLaMA-1 era (2023), with 2048-token context.
- Requires logit access: LSR scores need p_LM(y|c ◦ x) and the ensemble uses per-chunk output probabilities. Hosted chat APIs rarely give these (inference from the method; the paper does not discuss APIs).
- LSR top-10 chunks and scores were computed once with LLaMA 65B and DRAGON+ and not refreshed during R-ft.
- Retrieval queries come from hand-written templates (Tables 10 and 12). The authors defer "automatically generating task-specific retrieval queries to future work."
- Dev-set tuning: hyperparameters were selected on 6 KILT dev tasks. Only 4 of 10 eval tasks are genuinely few-shot, and "for the remaining tasks, we report few-shot results assuming access to in-domain development data."
- The ATLAS comparison is not matched. Model size, per-task vs single model, and the 64-shot recipe all differ. RA-DIT is footnoted as "compares favorably" to InstructRetro 48B, with different base LMs and data.
- The authors report lower 0-shot LLaMA numbers on NQ and TQA than Touvron et al. because they use exact match (footnote 7).
- HotpotQA multi-hop: the dense retriever "struggles to return useful text chunks", and larger LMs keep an advantage.
- No latency, cost or single-run variance or significance tests are reported. All results are single-run (none stated).
- Chunk concatenation fine-tuning and multi-step RA-DIT are left to future work.
- Dated: LLaMA 65B, DRAGON+, 2021 Wikipedia. No comparison to modern long-context or reasoning models.

BUILDS ON (as printed)
- REPLUG, Shi et al., 2023b (parallel retrieval ensembling and LSR objective, which RA-DIT generalises to multi-task data).
- DRAGON+, Lin et al., 2023 (initial retriever).
- Atlas, Izacard et al., 2022b (corpus dump, baseline).
- In-Context RALM, Ram et al., 2023.
- REALM (Guu et al., 2020); RETRO (Borgeaud et al., 2022); RAG (Lewis et al., 2020).
- Instruction tuning: Chung et al., 2022b; Iyer et al., 2022 (label-loss objective, document attention masking); Zhou et al., 2023 (LIMA, few fine-tuning steps).
- Contrasted with Self-RAG (Asai et al., 2023), SAIL (Luo et al., 2023) and InstructRetro (Wang et al., 2023).

CODE
No code in the paper. It points to scripts at https://github.com/facebookresearch/RA-DIT for indexing and prompt generation. Load-bearing formulas (p.3-5):
- Mixture: pLM(y|x,C') = Σ_{c∈C'} pLM(y|c ◦ x) · pR(c|x), with pR a softmax of s(x,c) over the top-k.
- LSR target: pLSR(c|x,y) = exp(pLM(y|c ◦ x)/τ) / Σ_{c'} exp(pLM(y|c' ◦ x)/τ).
- Loss: L(DR) = E KL(pR(c|x) ‖ pLSR(c|x,y)).
- Prompt format: "Background: {retrieved passage}\n\nQ: {question}\nA: {answer}"

FIGURES
- Fig. 1 (p.2): RA-DIT separately fine-tunes the LLM (LM-ft: maximise answer likelihood given retrieval-augmented prompt) and the retriever (R-ft: minimise KL to the LLM's preference). It shows the two-stage design at a glance. I did not view the image.
- Fig. 2 (p.22): RA-IT performance at 7B, 13B and 65B on dev tasks, with 0-shot dashed and 5-shot solid. It shows that retrieval helps small models more. I did not view the image, and the data are not in the extracted text.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found.
- Tables are flattened text, but the rows read cleanly. The Table 2 relative percentages in the intro do not match its point differences (see the NQ claim).
- Table 5's first rows are labelled "DRAGON+" and similar. Its "⋄ Avg" column is the average over 6 KILT dev tasks. Table 6 uses "RIT" where the text says RA-IT.
- The Table 7 DRAGON+ row (53.4) does not equal Table 6's baseline (53.8) because of few-shot truncation differences (footnote 11). Compare only within a table.
